source.title: Vanishing Curvature and the Power of Adaptive Methods in Randomly Initialized Deep Networks
source.authors: Antonio Orvieto; Jonas Köhler; Dario Pavllo; T. Hofmann; Aurélien Lucchi

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports training-accuracy outcomes for randomly initialized deep networks on CIFAR-10, but its main analysis concerns gradient and curvature magnitudes rather than the claim’s training-error measure.
record.gate_note: Training-accuracy results are reported for a 500-layer stripped ResNet on CIFAR-10 and for a 128-layer Fashion-MNIST MLP. Gradient and Hessian magnitude results do not directly measure the claim’s training-classification-error outcome and are not cataloged as rows. The paper cites results from other studies; those cited results are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study gives a specific theoretical argument limiting V4: activation-matched Xavier and He initialization can preserve expected propagation norms while typical signals, gradients and curvature vanish when width is too small relative to depth. It also reports failure of SGD to train a 500-layer CIFAR-10 classifier.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate but incomplete. The authors argue that vanishing gradients co-occur with vanishing curvature, making flat initialization plateaus difficult for SGD to escape; effective width and architecture determine this failure mode, and adaptive methods can overcome it. RMSprop trains the tested 500-layer stripped ResNet but heavily overfits.
record.recipe_differences: The CIFAR-10 training comparison uses He initialization, a stripped ResNet without batch normalization or residual connections, and RMSprop or SGD. The study does not test the full range of recipes in the claim.
record.method_sensitivity: On the 500-layer CIFAR-10 model, reported training accuracy differs by optimizer; the SGD learning rates tested are 1e-3, 1e-6, and 1e-9.

fits_no_version.finding: RMSprop trains the 500-layer stripped ResNet where SGD fails.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Adaptive optimization can overcome flat initialization plateaus in very deep networks without normalization or residual shortcuts.

fits_no_version.finding: Removing either batch normalization or shortcuts produces exploding initialization gradients in the tested ResNets.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Initialization-gradient stability in these architectures depends on combining normalization and residual connections.

record.problems: The relevant CIFAR-10 training-accuracy outcomes are presented in plots without exact values in the text. The study reports 10 random seeds and 95% confidence intervals. Its CIFAR-10 training setup is image reconstruction with mean-squared-error loss, despite the figure labeling the outcome as accuracy.
record.rows_left_out: No other training-accuracy rows were extracted. Fashion-MNIST results concern a different dataset and are not mapped to the CIFAR-specific V1 version. Gradient and Hessian magnitude measurements do not directly measure training classification error.

untested.parts: CIFAR-100, corrupted or random labels, Adam on CIFAR-10, and systematic comparisons of model size, early stopping or regularization.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student spurious-minimum frequencies and the effect of one or two extra student neurons.
Training-error comparisons across depths for matched plain batch-normalized and residual convolutional networks; special tanh initialization and Fixup training.
Direct training-speed comparisons between activation-matched and unmatched initializations; deep tanh orthogonal-versus-Gaussian training and 10,000-layer orthogonal convolutional training.
Recovery above the initial linearized stability limit, catapult trajectories and full-batch edge-of-stability dynamics.
Accuracy gain per training time and learning-rate tolerance with versus without batch normalization; matched Fixup comparisons.

missing.what: A record of the specific theoretical qualification to activation-matched initialization: stable expectations can coexist with vanishing typical propagation, with width relative to depth governing the limitation. Existing exclusions of gradient measurements do not capture this argument.
missing.locator: Section 3, Propositions 3–5 and Theorem 6; Section 4, Theorem 9 and discussion of Xavier and He initialization

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source of any version. Initialization-gradient and Hessian measurements alone do not establish V3's training-error comparison or V6's acceleration claim. Figure 8's classification outcome should not be recast as reconstruction merely because separate convolutional experiments use image-to-image MSE.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR-100, corrupted or random labels, Adam, smaller-model comparisons, early stopping, and regularized recipes are not tested. The CIFAR-10 result uses RMSprop and SGD.
